selecting off can produce HTTP 400. - **After:** The request sends adaptive thinking with output_config.effort set to low; the recorded live probe completed with OK. ## Review scores | Measure | Result | What it means | |---|---|---| | **Overall readiness** | 🐚 platinum hermit **(4/6)** | A focused, useful patch with repaired replay findings, live provider-contract evidence, and meaningful builder coverage; proof does not include a full shipped CLI or Gateway flow. | | **Proof confidence** | 🐚 platinum hermit **(4/6)** | Sufficient (live_output): Recorded live output exercises the registered MiniMax wrapper and real Anthropic streaming client against the CN endpoint with a 256-token cap: low and max both sent adaptive thinking with the selected effort and completed with OK; live evidence covers low/max API-key requests, while OAuth and signed replay use the real-builder harness.
Agent review details ### How this fits together MiniMax provider hooks receive model metadata, conversation history, and generation options, then prepare requests for the shared Anthropic client and return streamed assistant responses. ```mermaid flowchart LR A[Agent or simple completion] --> B[MiniMax provider hooks] B --> C[M3.1 effort normalization] C --> D[Anthropic history conversion] D --> E[Adaptive payload and output cap] E --> F[MiniMax API] F --> G[Assistant response] ``` ### Technical review Best possible solution: Keep the M3.1 profile and request shaping in the MiniMax plugin while preserving signed history, output caps, and existing M3/M2 behavior. Do we have a high-confidence way to reproduce the issue? Current-main source exposes off/adaptive for M3.1 and lacks its effort translation; independent released-version reports confirm HTTP 400 for disabled thinking, but this read-only review ran no target code. Is this the best way to solve the issue? The existing provider hooks are the appropriate boundary, and the current producer repair preserves replay before conversion rather than attempting to restore lost history afterward. AGENTS.md: found and applied where relevant. ([`extensions/minimax/thinking.ts:10`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/c44c2e51ad3fdeaa84a0aa35a36c4f83a116c746/extensions/minimax/thinking.ts#L10), [c44c2e51ad3f](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/c44c2e51ad3fdeaa84a0aa35a36c4f83a116c746)) - **Replay repairs verified in source:** The wrapper supplies calculation allowance before history conversion, ignores manual thinking budgets, and restores requested/configured output caps in the final payload. ([`extensions/minimax/stream.ts:25`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/90114e616e18c16b27abda7d0ef7bc97e28934aa/extensions/minimax/stream.ts#L25), [90114e616e18](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/90114e616e18c16b27abda7d0ef7bc97e28934aa)) - **Actual replay boundary:** The Anthropic builder decides whether to retain signed thinking before invoking the payload hook, confirming why normalization must precede conversion. ([`extensions/minimax/index.test.ts:493`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/90114e616e18c16b27abda7d0ef7bc97e28934aa/extensions/minimax/index.test.ts#L493), [90114e616e18](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/90114e616e18c16b27abda7d0ef7bc97e28934aa)) - **Provider contract and independent reports:** The open canonical issue https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/160037 includes php737's five-effort live captures; olveww-dot reports the disabled-thinking rejection on 2026.9.9. MiniMax's current documentation confirms mandatory thinking and the five effort values: [Anthropic API contract](https://platform.minimax.io/docs/api-reference/text-anthropic-api). - **Maintainer-supported repair:** RomneyDa's MEMBER-associated request explicitly asks for review of the repaired current head and describes preserving signed replay and wire caps; no additional product approval is needed for those repairs. ### 2026.9.9 (current release) still affected — reproducible, with a verified workaround

Adding field evidence since this PR has been open 11 days with no maintainer review. Raising this only because the report is about the **shipped** release, not just `main`.

**Environment**
- OpenClaw **2026.9.9 (bcfc888)**, macOS 27.0.0 (Darwin) arm64
- npm-global install, npm 11.12.1, Node v24.15.0
- Provider: minimax, `https://api.minimaxi.com/anthropic/v1`

**Reproduction** — direct `POST /messages` against the configured provider, Anthropic-style, everything else identical between the two probes:

| model | `thinking` | result |
|---|---|---|
| `MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Preview` | `{"type":"disabled"}` | **HTTP 400** |
| `MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Preview` | *(field omitted)* | HTTP 200 |
| `MiniMax-M3` | `{"type":"disabled"}` | **HTTP 200** |

Provider response for the failing case:

```json
{"type":"error","error":{"type":"invalid_request_error","message":"invalid params, model \"MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Preview\" requires adaptive thinking; thinking.type=\"disabled\" (including reasoning.effort=none) is not allowed (2013)"}}
```

**User impact on 9.9:** the `openclaw` tool is entirely unavailable — system setup, repair, and config paths all fail with `OpenClaw requires working inference: LLM request failed: provider rejected the request schema or tool payload.` The same request without a `thinking` field succeeds, so the failure is specific to how thinking is translated, not to the model or the endpoint.

**Verified workaround:** setting the primary model to `MiniMax-M3` makes the disabled-thinking path work again (HTTP 200 above), so users on 9.9 are not blocked while this waits to merge. I did not patch `dist/` — the injected value lives below the setup-inference layer and I did not want to hand-maintain a local modification that the next update would discard.

This is not a request to change priority; just evidence that the gap persists in the current release rather than only in the revision this PR was first opened against.
